hook.en: Two girls, on two different continents, about a hundred years apart. Both discover as children that society treats their people unfairly.

objectives.en: Explain why the two extracts are paired

narration.en: Two girls, on two different continents, about a hundred years apart. Both discover as children that society treats their people unfairly.

body.en: "Memories of Childhood" brings together two autobiographical extracts. The first is by Zitkala-Sa, the pen name of Gertrude Simmons Bonnin, a Native American writer and activist who fought against the injustice done to her people. The second is by Bama, a Tamil Dalit writer, from her autobiography "Karukku", which describes the caste discrimination she faced.

points.en: Zitkala-Sa: Native American writer and activist

narration.en: "Memories of Childhood" brings together two autobiographical extracts. The first is by Zitkala-Sa, the pen name of Gertrude Simmons Bonnin, a Native American writer and activist who fought against the injustice done to her people. The second is by Bama, a Tamil Dalit writer, from her autobiography "Karukku", which describes the caste discrimination she faced.
We compare the two writers in a T-chart.

say.en: We compare Zitkala-Sa and Bama side by side.
Zitkala-Sa was Native American; Bama is a Tamil Dalit writer.
One was at a boarding school in America, the other at a village school in Tamil Nadu.
One faced racial and cultural oppression, the other caste discrimination.
Zitkala-Sa struggles but is overpowered; Bama chooses education.
Both grew up to write and resist.

explanation.en: Different cultures, places and times, but both women first felt injustice as children and later fought it through writing.

body.en: The two women come from very different cultures, places and times, yet both belong to communities pushed to the margins of society. Both recall a moment in childhood when they first felt this injustice, and both grew up to resist it through education and writing. The extracts show that marginalisation exists across the world.

problem.en: Why are the extracts by Zitkala-Sa and Bama placed together?

steps.en: Both are autobiographical accounts of childhood.
Both writers come from marginalised communities.
Both describe their first experience of injustice and resistance.

answer.en: Both extracts are autobiographical and describe the childhood of women from marginalised communities, one Native American and one Dalit. Though separated by place and time, each recalls first realising the injustice done to her people and each resists it.
